meta.title: TEDROX Documents — local-first document toolbox
meta.description: Process PDFs, documents, spreadsheets, images and conversions locally. Offline. Fast. Open source under the MIT license.
hero.title: One app for the files you actually work with.
hero.subtitle: Edit, convert, merge, inspect and export documents locally — without sending your files to random websites.
demo.caption: Real output from the tdx-doc CLI. No upload, no account, no queue.
features.title: A workbench, not a widget
features.subtitle: Thirty focused tools across five areas, sharing one engine and one job queue.
feature.pdf.title: PDF workstation
feature.pdf.desc: Merge, split, extract, reorder, rotate and clean PDFs. Compress embedded images, edit metadata, watermark documents and build PDFs from images.
feature.documents.title: Documents
feature.documents.desc: Create and convert DOCX through the native OOXML engine. Markdown, plain text and HTML to PDF with system font embedding.
feature.sheets.title: Spreadsheets & CSV
feature.sheets.desc: A real CSV workbench: delimiter and encoding detection, type inference, filtering, sorting, deduplication, splitting, joining, CSV ↔ XLSX ↔ JSON.
feature.images.title: Image Lab
feature.images.desc: Convert between PNG, JPEG, WebP, BMP, TIFF and AVIF. Resize, crop, rotate, strip metadata, render SVG, trace raster to vector, build ICO icons.
feature.convert.title: Conversion center
feature.convert.desc: One route from input to output with an honest capability registry. Unsupported conversions stay disabled instead of failing silently.
feature.jobs.title: Job runtime
feature.jobs.desc: Every operation runs as a cancellable job with staged progress, bounded concurrency, atomic writes and verified output.
formats.title: Supported formats
formats.pdf: Open, inspect, merge, split, extract, delete, reorder, rotate, compress, watermark, metadata, privacy clean, images to PDF.
formats.documents.title: Documents
formats.documents.desc: DOCX, Markdown, TXT, HTML, RTF inspection. Legacy DOC through the optional LibreOffice adapter.
formats.sheets.title: Spreadsheets
formats.sheets.desc: CSV, TSV, XLSX, XLS and ODS reading; XLSX writing; CSV ↔ XLSX ↔ JSON conversion.
formats.images.title: Images
formats.images.desc: PNG, JPEG, WebP, BMP, TIFF, AVIF, GIF, SVG, ICO. SVG rasterization and vector tracing for logos and line art.
privacy.title: Your files stay on your machine
privacy.noUpload.title: No upload
privacy.noUpload.desc: Processing happens in the local native core. There is no server component and no account.
privacy.noTelemetry.title: No telemetry
privacy.noTelemetry.desc: No analytics, no crash reporting, no tracking. Logs contain operation metadata only, never document contents.
privacy.atomic.title: Safe writes
privacy.atomic.desc: Outputs are written to a temporary file, flushed, verified and only then moved into place. Source files are never overwritten by default.
privacy.honest.title: Honest limits
privacy.honest.desc: No “lossless 90% compression” promises. PDF rendering to images requires the optional PDFium adapter, and the UI says so.
cli.title: Scriptable from day one
cli.subtitle: The same engine that powers the app is available as a command line tool with JSON output and clean exit codes.
cli.note: Progress is disabled automatically when the output is piped. Ctrl+C cancels cooperatively.
download.title: Download
download.subtitle: Builds are published on GitHub Releases. Version
download.windows.desc: Portable ZIP with the tdx-doc CLI and desktop build.
download.linux.desc: Build from source with cargo; AppImage and .deb packages are on the roadmap.
download.android.desc: Native Android shell is in development; the shared core is ready for it.
download.source.title: Source
download.source.desc: MIT licensed Rust workspace. Build everything with cargo.
download.note: SHA256 checksums are attached to every release. Code signing is not configured yet, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run.
faq.title: FAQ
faq.a1: No. All processing happens locally in the native Rust core. The application has no server component and requires no account.
faq.q2: How is this different from online converters?
faq.a2: Speed, privacy and reliability. There are no queues, no file size limits imposed by someone else's server, and no documents sitting in a temporary cloud folder.
faq.q3: Which licenses do the dependencies use?
faq.a3: The core targets permissive licenses only (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC, Zlib, MPL-2.0). LibreOffice and PDFium are optional external adapters, never bundled, and are documented in THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md.
faq.q4: Can I use it in scripts and CI?
faq.a4: Yes. tdx-doc returns stable exit codes, supports --json everywhere and works without any GUI. See docs/cli.md.
footer.built: Built with a shared Rust core. MIT licensed.
